title: No door says whether opening a store would migrate it, so the commit gate's view-skew check keeps a second copy of Store::init's decision
body:
## What happens

ST0095 WP-03 gives the commit gate's view-skew check a store guard (AC-03.1). The check is `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/thread_view_skew_check.sh`. Before its `doctor` opens this checkout's store, the guard:

1. reads the store schema the build writes, from the header of a scratch store that build made;
2. reads the checkout store's schema from its header;
3. judges a copy of `intent/` when the checkout's store is older or has none.

So a dev build never migrates the main store at a commit.

That comparison restates `Store::init`'s decision, in `native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/store.rs`: an older store migrates, an equal one opens, a newer one is refused. The guard learns the build's schema by having it make a store, because no door says either thing without opening a store for write. The script's comment calls the block a second copy kept for want of a door. critic-shell found that nothing owned the door, in WP-03's review under vc decision 133, at Highlander severity.

## What it costs

- One decision has two homes. A change to when `Store::init` migrates is not seen by the script.
- The guard covers only one of the gate's two `doctor` runs. The shipped half runs `intent doctor` through PATH (`lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh`). While brew is first on PATH, that is the release. `intent use dev` points it at the dev build instead, which then opens and migrates the main store before the script runs.
- vc decision 132 keeps seats on brew, but that is a rule, not a check. Every verb run by hand with a dev build is outside the script too.

## The fix

The binary needs a door. Its meaning is cc's and its shape is ic's. Any one of these would do:

- the build's store schema as a row of `intent schema --versions`, so the script stops making a store to learn it;
- a `doctor` mode that refuses where opening the store would migrate it, so the script stops comparing;
- the migrate arm behind an explicit opt-in, so no build migrates a store unasked. This also covers the shipped half and every verb.

Then delete `schema_in` and the comparison from the script, as its comment says.

Found by critic-shell on ST0095 WP-03's diff, 2026-11-19.
